meta.title: Send to E-Reader (Demo)
meta.description: Send posts to your e-reader as ePub files, by email or direct download. Works standalone or integrates with the Friends plugin. Pre-loaded with a handful of posts and two configured e-readers, so the row and bulk actions on the Posts screen work right away.
meta.author: Alex Kirk

steps.code:
'Why an ePub beats a browser tab', 'content' => "

A reading list that lives in browser tabs is a reading list you will never finish. The tabs are on the wrong device, they reflow badly on a small screen, and every one of them is one notification away from being closed.

\n\n

An ePub is the opposite. It is a single file, it is finished the moment it is built, and the device it lands on has one job. There is no address bar to wander off into.

\n\n

The trick is getting the article out of the browser and onto the device without a cable, a conversion service, or a second account. That is the whole problem this plugin solves.

", ), array( 'title' => 'What goes into the file', 'content' => "

Each post becomes one chapter. The chapter opens with the post title, carries the byline and the permalink, and then the post content itself, converted to XHTML so that the e-reader's renderer accepts it without complaint.

\n\n

Images in the post body are pulled into the file rather than linked, including the ones hosted on the same site. That matters on a device that spends most of its life offline: an article whose illustrations are missing is usually an article that no longer makes sense.

\n\n

Select several posts and they become several chapters in one file, with a title page in front. One file, one transfer, one thing to find on the device.

", ), array( 'title' => 'Sending to more than one device', 'content' => "

Most people end up with more than one place to send things: the e-reader by the bed, a tablet, and a plain download for everything else.

\n\n

Configure each of them once on the E-Readers screen. From then on the Posts screen offers one row action and one bulk action per device, so choosing where an article goes is a single click rather than a trip back through the settings.

\n\n

Delivery goes through WordPress's own mail, so whatever the site already uses to send mail is what carries the file.

", ), array( 'title' => 'A long one, for testing pagination', 'content' => "

Short posts do not tell you much about how a file will read on a device. This one is deliberately longer, so the chapter runs over several screens and you can see how headings, lists and quotes survive the trip.

\n\n

Headings

\n\n

A heading should still look like a heading after conversion, and it should not collide with the paragraph underneath it.

\n\n

A smaller heading

\n\n

Nested headings are where converters usually start to disagree with each other.

\n\n

Lists

\n\n
  • An unordered list, with a first item that runs on a little longer than the others so that at least one item has to wrap.
  • A shorter one.
  • And a third.
\n\n
  1. An ordered list.
  2. Because numbering is its own kind of trouble.
\n\n

Quotes and code

\n\n

A block quote, indented, and long enough that it wraps onto a second line on a phone-sized screen.

\n\n

Inline code should stay monospaced, and a block should keep its line breaks:

\n\n
wp send-to-e-reader --help
\n\n

The end

\n\n

If everything above survived, the rest of your posts almost certainly will too.

", ), array( 'title' => 'One that is already sent', 'content' => "

The plugin remembers which posts it has already put on a device, so a second pass over the same list can skip them.

\n\n

This post is marked as already sent, so you can see how that looks before sending anything yourself.

", ), ); $post_ids = array(); foreach ( $posts as $index => $post ) { $post_ids[] = wp_insert_post( array( 'post_title' => $post['title'], 'post_content' => $post['content'], 'post_status' => 'publish', 'post_type' => 'post', 'post_author' => 1, 'post_date' => gmdate( 'Y-m-d H:i:s', time() - ( ( count( $posts ) - $index ) * DAY_IN_SECONDS ) ), ) ); } // Mark the last one as already sent so the "already sent" state is visible. update_post_meta( end( $post_ids ), 'sent-to-ereader', time() - HOUR_IN_SECONDS ); // Add a second e-reader next to the "Download ePub" one the activation hook // creates, so that the per-e-reader row and bulk actions are visible. if ( class_exists( 'Send_To_E_Reader\E_Reader_Kindle' ) ) { $option = 'send-to-e-reader_readers'; $ereaders = get_option( $option, array() ); $kindle = new Send_To_E_Reader\E_Reader_Kindle( 'My Kindle', 'demo@free.kindle.com' ); $kindle->active = true; $id = $kindle->get_id(); if ( $id ) { $ereaders[ $id ] = $kindle; update_option( $option, $ereaders ); } }
